utterances.text: Could we slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, we can read it later on. You have no objection, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection to having it marked for identification. I'd just like to observe that it's not clear from the title of the document, which itself is only partly legible, but even if it were legible, it's not entirely clear which authority produced this document and the accused has put his case to the witness, no objection to that, but he has also contextualised this document in his own submissions which is an issue which we may wish to return to at some other point. I'm just raising it at this point. But no objection in principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you not say that this was part of the previous document or annex of it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first document is a letter to the municipality, and the second document is also signed by inhabitants of Renovica of Serb ethnicity on the 25th of June. They made submissions as to what they had lost to the municipality which failed to protect them. They are submitting a reckoning of what they lost. You can look at the last page. It says exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Doraiswamy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D20, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, you mentioned that in Pale life was very hard for Muslims and they were unable to buy what they wanted to buy in the amounts they wanted. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to call up 1D810.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have both versions. The date is 24 April. It says: "Agency 'SRNA' was authorised by the Pale Crisis Staff to announce the following: "In the interest of controlling prices in the Pale region, all wholesale trade shall be conducted exclusively through the trade enterprise 'Veleprom' Pale. "Retail shops privately and socially owned shall be supplied exclusively through this company. "The sale prices of articles have to be identical and clearly labelled, as well as information regarding available quantities. "The shops that fail to abide by this role shall be closed down." You didn't mention later -- earlier that everyone felt restrictions of food and that the prices were controlled by the municipalities. You said it only applied to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what would you say if you read on the window of a shop that there are no goods for non-Serbs? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would ask why didn't you state that earlier.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which shop was that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Korani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which one in Korani?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are not many shops in Korani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, I have to tell you there is an old rule from Roman law altera pars which means listen to the other side as well. I should have known this much earlier, and there will be a response. Let's try to avoid claims like some Serbs did something to some Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As a general matter, I think the accused should refrain from giving directions to the witness. I think that's more the task of the Presiding Judge, and the Presiding Judge has control over the questioning of the witness. The accused should refrain from the comments such as those which he's just made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I tend to agree with it. Mr. Karadzic, bear that in mind. Just -- why don't you just put your questions. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with that too, but I wasn't giving instructions. I just wanted to explain why I was insisting on accuracy and precision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This report that agency "SRNA" made on the authority of the government in Pale to the effect that prices and quantities of goods available are restricted for all buyers, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw this announcement before while I was living in Pale, but it was basically first come, first served. And if we had no food left at home, only then would we go to a shop. I mostly went if I was out of cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D21, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call now 1D815.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We see the document now, "suppressing smuggling at Pale." The date is the 2nd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May? Is it May? Yes, yes, we can see from the translation that it's May: "Many citizens are calling the 'SRNA' agency and begging us to do something to stop the smuggling and the illegal raising of prices of various goods. We are, therefore, once again publishing the decision of the Pale Crisis Staff that all wholesale trade must be conducted through the trade enterprise 'Velprom' in Pale." You know about that enterprise?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was state-owned at the time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Retail shops privately and socially owned shall be supplied exclusively through this company. "The sale prices of products have to be identical and visibly indicated and so must the information regarding available quantities." Do you agree that this is a measure against those who wanted to make profit at the expense of poor people?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smuggling has not stopped to this day, let alone then. They still haven't managed to put a stop to thieves who steal cars, disassemble them, and sell spare parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why this was issued by the authorities in Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document 1D815 and to call up new document 1D809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D22.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D809.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have it now in English and in Serbian. It's again 24 May: "The 'SRNA' agency is under obligation to publish the announcement made by the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Pale. "In the municipality of Pale and all the regions that have joined the municipality, the regular supply of food and other staples has been restored at very favourable prices for all shops. "There will be enough food in the future as well, and citizens do not need to create crowds. "Consumers are encouraged to report unauthorised increases in prices at the following numbers ..." and so forth. Third paragraph: "All owners of tractors, lawn mowers, and motor vehicles from the municipality of Pale are informed that they should report to their community offices in order to receive a confirmation, a certificate, to enable them to buy fuel. "All men who had fled to the area of Pale between 18 and 60 years of age are hereby informed to immediately report to the secretariat for national defence." Next item: "On the territory of the municipality of Pale, not a single incident has occurred until now or an unlawful break-in and entering, as was the case in Sarajevo. Should any incident occur, the perpetrator shall be taken to the court in Pale and be appropriately punished on the spot. "All industrial and social sectors are working normally in the municipality of Pale. The elementary school in Pale is full beyond capacity with students from Sarajevo. "Refugees are receiving food aid daily. "Citizens of all ethnicities are responding in large numbers to the call for donating blood." That's the last paragraph. Does this also reflect the situation in Pale in end May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. But when there was an attack in Zepa, young men from my street went to donate blood and were turned back. They were refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't know whether the blood bank had the resources to keep the blood donated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In any case, it says here that people of all ethnicities are responding. You are talking about Muslim young men?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but it happened after the attack on Zepa.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, do we have a number for this document, 1D809?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D23.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D808 is going to be our next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There it is. Dated 18 April 1992, two weeks into the war: "Agency 'SRNA' learned that on 17 April 1992 at 1645 hours, the first healthy baby was born in the newly opened general surgical hospital in the Serbian municipality of Pale." Let me digress here. Why was it called Serbian municipality of Pale? Do you remember that this name is used only if it was envisaged that the municipal -- that the Muslim municipality of Pale existed in parallel?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it was envisaged?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never involved in politics, but I know the Muslim municipality did not exist at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So: " ... in the newly opened general surgical ward in the Serbian municipality of Pale, the first healthy baby was born. Nermina Causevic from Renovica gave birth to a healthy girl. "Even though labour was very complicated, everything ended well and the happy mother is recuperating in the hospital with all the necessary care." Is Nermina Causevic, judging by the name, a Muslim woman?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence, 1D808, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D24, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up Defence document 1D811, 811, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have the document in both versions. The here is the 26th of April, 1992, and there's another news agency report, and it says: "Today mothers and young women from Pale visited the wounded who are being treated in Koran. The women from Pale wished them happy Easter," so it's Easter here; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "... and a quick recovery and showed their concern for their health and welfare with presents that they presented them with. "The responsible official thanked these women from Pale for their visit and asked them to prevail upon their husbands and brothers not to shoot if there is no need, even if we're dealing with holidays, because shooting -- the sound of shooting upsets the people in hospital." Now, you mentioned the shooting that Muslims and Serbs went about when there was a celebration, and now we see this document and what it says there. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree or disagree. This is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you would agree that if there's shooting it upsets people in hospital?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D25, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like 1D823 to be called up next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The date is the 25th of May, 1992, it's an order from the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Pale. It says: "Based on a request made by the command of the armed forces of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Pale, at its session held on the 25th of May, issued an order that the work of catering businesses, bars, and cafes be temporarily suspended. This order excludes catering facilities serving food, but they are prohibited temporarily from serving alcohol as well." The rest isn't important, but do you remember that there were these restrictions and limitations on the work of cafes and restaurants and bars and the issuance of alcohol?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you about life in Pale as I knew it, and I know these cafes and bars very well, the main ones in the centre. And I can tell you that civilians went there and soldiers went there while I was living there, and I was expelled in 1992 on the 2nd of July. Up until then, the cafes and bars in the centre were working, they were open.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was on the 25th of May, which means one week prior to your departure -- you left in July; is that right? I apologise. I got the dates mixed up.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence, 1D823, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection to this either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D26.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, I want to ask you something now. Have you had -- did you have enough of us politicians on television? Did you have enough of seeing our faces on your television screens and so on and everything we were saying?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll be quite frank. If the people could do anything, then they wouldn't have allowed you anywhere near the media in Bosnia or near the press or near any kind of electronic media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But whatever we said they would broadcast; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Whatever you did, you did something that was bad for the people. What worse thing in the world is there than war, as far as the population is concerned? And that's what you were engaged in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree, but I just want to know whether the media were interested in Izetbegovic, myself, Kljuc, the leaders of the three ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to tell you what the journalists did. Yes, they did interview you all the time, but the people didn't want you, let me tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D831, please. It's a document that is being translated, but I'm going to put a few paragraphs to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It concerns an event related to Zlovrh. You mentioned this in your statement, I believe, and in your testimony as well?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention Zlovrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I mean the crisis, the incident that took place, you mentioned that. And this piece of news -- or rather, it's a report of some kind from the commander of a unit which went to Zlovrh. His name was Suka, Dragan. I'm going to read out a few paragraphs: "On the 2nd of June, 1992, I was called by the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Republic of BH, through Colonel Veljko Bosanac. I was told to report to Major-General Manojlo Milovanovic in order to be issued my assignment. At the time I was in Praca, and I set out to take on my assignment. I reported to Major-General Milovanovic, and in the presence of Major-General Gvero, Djukic, and some other officers, he issued the following order to me: He said that on the 4th of June, 1992, I was to go to Zlovrh, a military repeater station there, to hand over water, food, and ammunition for 32 persons, to last them one month. At the time at Zlovrh, there were two officers and ten soldiers. And I was supposed to provide 20 more men to provide security." I'd now like to skip the next part and move on to paragraph 3. "I informed him about my activities and he said that I should prepare to carry out my assignment. In the hallway, I came across the chief of the traffic service and asked him to provide me with ten soldiers that I needed to carry out my assignment. The head of the traffic service asked General Milovanovic if that was okay and if he could -- but he said that he could not provide me with ten soldiers. I was told that I was not allowed to fire a single bullet because everything had been decided and agreed upon with the other side and that only food, water, and fuel should be transported there. I returned to Pale at 2100 hours. And then on the 4th of June, I went to the unit." This is a rather epic rendition, rather long. But on page 2, it goes on to say, after describing the route they had taken, he said: "We went past the village Stoborani, on the left bank."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Karadzic. What is the point of reading out the whole document? What is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, I'm just reading excerpts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this particular paragraph, Mr. Suka is explaining what happened to him en route and the agreement made with the Muslim side from Zepa. He said that the bridge was de-mined and that they moved on. He says: "When I reached the bridge, snipers opened fire and I was the main target of attack. My driver was wounded on the occasion and all-out fighting broke out." And we can now move on to page 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, put your question. We are here to hear evidence of Mr. Crncalo, not Mr. Suka. If necessary, you can call him. You can put the content, in a brief manner, of the statement to Mr. Crncalo, as you did, but there's no point of going through all the content of it, reading out in the transcript. And you can admit -- you can tender the document if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, you said that 45 soldiers were killed in this incident, of which 40 were from Pale; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never mentioned any numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it is the large group and the many killings that took place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the helicopters brought in the dead and wounded, but I didn't know the numbers. I didn't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm talking about the event you mentioned as having seen and heard me address these families.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender 1D831 and then I have two more questions to ask based on that document, for identification, of course, because it's being translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, we object to the admission of this. This is a statement of Dragan Suka and the correct route for admission, as Your Honours have already ruled, is 92 bis or 92 ter. I also note in passing that it's not signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Same rule, Mr. Karadzic, if you like to tender this into evidence, you can call him later on. But you can put the crux of the statement to the witness, but we will not admit it. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, this was a moment of crisis with a lot of tension; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A large-scale funeral; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the funeral myself, but, yes, I just happened to see the gathering of people as I was passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were about 10 metres away from me; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a little further away, maybe 50 metres, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But would you see me about in Pale otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the first time that I saw you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Crncalo, how is it possible that I said anything in an open space without it being broadcast in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you ask your people that, the people who accompanied you and all the people who broadcast your statements and announcements generally. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But what I want to say is - and you confirmed this - the media, especially at Pale, would broadcast and publish everything I said and everything the other prominent politicians said. So how is it possible for me to say something as drastic as you say I said here without ever anybody having recorded it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how that was possible, but that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to object to the form of the question. The question said that the witness had confirmed an item of evidence, and I'd ask the accused to identify when that was confirmed. I don't think the witness confirmed that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In today's transcript, on page 55, line 17, when I put an introductory question to the witness and asked whether the media were interested in my activities and whether they followed them closely. And the witness's answer was to confirm that, that I was constantly in the news. I'd now like to make things more precise to help the Prosecution out. It was a statement given in Sarajevo on the 23rd of August, 1995, where you, Mr. Crncalo, did not mention that important sentence which I allegedly uttered; that is to say that the best way to protect Serb houses was to attack Muslim houses. You never ever stated that anywhere else before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you think that I thought this up, then just look through the tapes and transcripts, and I believe that the Tribunal has that too, that in other places you also said, Let's attack Muslim houses, attack Muslim houses, and by doing so you'll be defending your own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Crncalo, the question was whether you told the authorities that on 23rd of August that Mr. Karadzic said to attack Muslim houses. Do you remember whether you said that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, on one occasion, in one of my statements, I did mention that, but I can't give you an exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, not only in the statement of the 23rd of August, 1995, not only did you not mention it there, but you didn't mention it during the -- your testimony in the Krajisnik trial, on transcript page 5294 and 5327 and 5342 in the Krajisnik trial, where you mentioned the event. You don't mention a single word about my having said that; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't testify against you. This is the first time that I'm testifying against you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you. So you prepared yourself especially for me, did you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I prepare myself especially? I just rely on my memory, what I remember, and I give statements on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to call up document 1D854, please. 1D854 is the minutes and tape-recording, and this is the transcript of that recording from the 17th Session of the People's Assembly held on the 24th to the 26th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we have it. On page 2 of this document, you have part of my speech recorded, and a quarter of the Muslims had already left, three-quarters remained. Now, here is what I say in that speech at this Assembly session, and I'm addressing the deputies, the Assembly members. And it's paragraph 3: "As for the first item on the agenda, the president of the Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina will be speaking about the political war time situation in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," so that the president of the Assembly is asking me to take the floor. And now I'd like to move on to page 3 because we can skip this interjectory part. I don't want to tire the Trial Chamber and the participants with that section, but if we move on to page 3, at the beginning there, here is what I say: "It is with regret that I have to state that in Palama the Muslims do not want peace except in Bijeljina and in Pale where there are 20 per cent of them because nobody is touching them there, nor does anyone consider them to be second-rate citizens. But, on the contrary, our state officials are communicating with them trying to persuade them that they have no reason for fear and anxiety. So in Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Serbian people have gained their freedom and their state and they're willing to allow others to live alongside them. And I hope that during the Assembly we will make some conclusions and decisions to further invigorate this state." Do you see that part of the text and that part of my speech?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is well-known to the Prosecution and, therefore, I would like to tender this part of the transcript of the Assembly held in July. It is 1D854, so I'd like to tender 1D854 into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. But what was your question, Mr. Karadzic? After reading out this part, all you asked was whether you see that part of the text. What's the point of your question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point is, Your Excellency, that I wanted to hear from Mr. Crncalo how what he says tallies with this, which is the official policy of the state. And this was a closed session of the parliament. It was not known in advance that this transcript will ever become public.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, why were we then expelled from Pale? Just tell me. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. I'm just asking you how can what you say be possible, and we have no trace of that, no record, whereas for this we have a record? Our officials such as Koljevic are meeting citizens, although it would be quite enough for a municipal chief to meet with the citizens. But the vice-president of the state is here meeting with citizens to assure them that there is nothing to fear.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I'm saying is corroborated by what Koljevic said; namely, that Serbs don't want to live together with Muslims at Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on. What would be the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If it's convenient, shall we have a break now? We will have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, yesterday, on transcript page 74, you said that the Serb authorities pursued an active campaign for the expulsion of Muslims, or rather, to make Muslims leave Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did this campaign look like? How did it manifest itself? That is, in March while the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina still existed, who was the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Bakir Alispahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was also high up. It was actually Alija Delimustafic. And who was the minister of defence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not look into these political positions. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could it have been Jerko Doko, a Croat?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let it be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were very prominent Muslim senior staff Avdo Hebib, Munir Alispahic, Bakir Alispahic, Selmo Selimovic, and Alija Delimustafic in the MUP. Could you name one prominent Serb in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the first time I'm answering a question like this. I'm telling you again politics didn't interest me and politicians didn't interest me. I was interested in the regular life of a regular citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for record, Mr. Karadzic, what you cited is part of Mr. Gaynor's summary, not his evidence. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Excellency, but Mr. Gaynor asked for a confirmation and received it from the witness. So that is to be considered the evidence of this witness. I agree we should not delve into politics, but this is about the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the state authorities. Until the 6th of April, the state authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the MUP, especially, were full of prominent Muslim staff. There was only one Serb in charge of crime investigation. All the rest were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come then that something happened in Pale that nothing prevented -- that no one from the state authorities prevented or even published?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These problems started with your establishment of the Assembly of Republika Srpska. You were involved directly. You were a participant; I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move on. We'll discuss it with other people, when exactly Republika Srpska started to operate. Here is one document, 1D832, if we can call it up. 1D832. We have the Serbian and here is the English. This is the response of the Municipal Assembly of Pale, dated 11 April 1992, to the group of Muslim citizens of Pale. It was not intended for the media. It was not sent to anyone else. It was sent to the group that had presented certain demands. Here is what the text says: "Having taken into consideration your proposals of 10 April 1992," that means the day before, "the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Pale has concluded, as follows: "There is no reason for the Muslim population to panic or move out, the Serbian municipality of Pale shall offer full protection to all citizens of Pale, whatever their ethnicity or creed." It's just after this time that this lady gave birth to that child, and there were other activities showing that there was no discrimination whatsoever. Second paragraph: "The population on the territory of the Serbian municipality of Pale will continue to be supplied as before, taking care that supplies be provided equally to all parts of the municipality." Third paragraph: "In order to overcome any potential difficulties, the Crisis Staff hereby proposes that the same issues be agreed on by the inter-party commission composed of members of the Pale SDS and SDA parties." Have you -- were you part of this delegation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on more than one occasion I was part of the local delegation, but I was not involved in the way you suggest, in any negotiations between the SDS and the SDA. I was part of a delegation as a regular citizen. And now when you talk about this document that is on the screen now, why would someone be sending, at the same time, activists to work in town on the ground motivating people to move out?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know. This group addressed the authorities with the demand to be allowed to move out, and the authorities reply, Don't do that. Stay here. There is a poem written by Aleksa Santic that's called "Stay Here," you know, at the time of the Turks, the Ottoman Turk occupation.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why couldn't they guarantee our safety? Every time we had contacts with the officials of the Pale municipality, nobody was able to give us any guarantees of safety. That's the answer we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You received a reply in writing. The first paragraph says: "The Serbian municipality of Pale shall offer full protection to all citizens regardless of ethnicity or creed."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was never shown to a single Muslim in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have a witness statement from another Muslim, and we'll show it in due time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this Defence document, 1D832?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D28.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me remind you -- the date of this document was 11 April. And may I now call up 1D828. We have an English translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an agency report dated 16 of April, four days after that response to the group of citizens of Muslim ethnicity in Pale. This text says in the subheading: "Muslims in Pale municipality recognise the legal police force in the municipality, trust them, and ask to co-operate exclusively with them while controlling the area where they constitute the majority, claims the agency." And then the text goes: "The authorities and the police in the Serbian municipality of Pale have reached an agreement with the Muslim population from several villages in the municipality, whereby all problems will be resolved by agreement only, reports the 'SRNA' news agency." And this was reported by the "Glas" newspaper in Sarajevo. The text goes on to say: "Having defined the Muslim villages as Bare, Rakovica, Praca, and Podgrab, the agency stated that the Muslims in these villages had been guarantees of personal safety and security of their properties, as well as normal supplies and regular bus transport. "The Muslims in Pale municipality recognise the legal police in the municipality, trust them, and ask to co-operate exclusively with them in controlling the area where they constitute the majority, reports the agency." So this was the basis, the proposal was to have two police stations in every area, that Muslims policemen go into Muslim villages, Serbs to go into Serb villages, everyone to deal with their own criminals; is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were looking for safety in Pale municipality, guarantees of safety. Malko Koroman, chief of police, told us. As long as there is no Muslim in the police station of Stari Grad, there will be no Muslim policemen in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you understand and you see that the municipality of Stari Grad cheated on the agreement to have Serbs represented in the police of that municipality, but let's leave that aside. The text goes on: "'SRNA' agency also denied the news item broadcast on Sarajevo TV last night that Muslims working in the Kasindol hospital near Sarajevo had been denied access to the hospital. There are only three doctors working in the hospital and they are on duty, on call, around-the-clock. The director, therefore, calls upon all the employees to report to work as soon as possible." Did you know about this, that this was publicised in the media?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this, but I would like to comment on the second point, with your leave. On the 15th of May - and I mentioned it in my statement - was the day when Muslim workers in the Korani factory were not allowed to come in by the guard standing in the reception area. Muslims were turned back and Serbs were allowed in. I wasn't going into the factory, but I just ran into my manager. Let me give you a time indication. It was just after that incident in Renovica. I asked my manager, Milivoj Utaj [phoen], Boss, were we dismissed? And he says, No, I just don't want to take any risks. I don't want anyone to be shot in the back in the factory. For the time being, go home, let's wait and see. Muslims were not allowed to go into the factory at that time. That is a comment on this Kasindol hospital news item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I'm talking about the 11th and the 15th of April. What you're talking about was in May. We'll have to check that. Whatever you say, I will have to respond to and present evidence either through you or through another witness.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'm here at your disposal. Ask whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I propose that this document 1D832 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D29, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I also tender 828.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was it ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, I will now make a statement and corroborate it with documents, and I will ask you, in the form of a question, to give me your response. I maintain that both presidents of the Pale municipality and the entire municipality acted as a very responsible and careful authorities and so did the third president, Vojo Milutinovic, whom you, perhaps, know. They were very careful and they never discriminated against Muslims, they didn't distinguish between Muslims and Serbs. I'm talking about the authorities, not about individuals.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time covered by my statements, there was this younger man, Starcevic, I don't know his first name. He never told us a harsh word, but he also couldn't give us any guarantees. Whenever we asked him for assurances of safety, he would send us to the police chief, Malko Koroman. And Malko Koroman would say, Oh, it's a better idea to go back to him and ask the same. We were just going back and forth, from one to the other. You know better and you don't have to answer me, you know that power was in the hands at that time of the Crisis Staff most probably. Neither of these two men dared give any guarantees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, the president of the municipality does not have command over the police. The police is commanded by the police commander under the supervision of the chief of the police station, Mr. Koroman. So the president of the municipality says, Go to the competent people whose job it is. And this Mr. Cvoro, on behalf of the municipality, provides guarantees, saying, Everything will be all right. Now, let me ask you, why were you living in fear and experiencing restrictions when you were so close, 15 metres away from the president of the republic in war time? Could you -- were you not able to kill me?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a killer, I never even thought about it. As far as restrictions go and the fear, if you had walked through Pale and run into those young men gone completely berserk, armed to their teeth with knives this size, bare above the waist, red ribbons around their forearms and around their foreheads, they were driving coupes armed with automatic guns, who would not fear them? How can you say we were not under pressure and living in fear? Anyone who says that is out of their mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were they people from Pale or some strangers?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know the size of Pale. I cannot recognise every single person. One night, one of my work colleagues was on a patrol. The person who was his partner moved towards me, probably to arrest me, and this work colleague of mine told him, Don't touch him. This is one of our locals, a quiet man. And I had just been on an errand to buy cigarettes and when I came home I told my wife, I almost got arrested and taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, are we of different races? Could we -- could anyone looking at us tell that one of us is a Serb, the other is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? You are from Montenegro; I am from Bosnia. My parents, grandparents, and great-grandparents lived and died in Bosnia. They always lived in peace with their Serb neighbours. There had never been any friction. People were more careful and eager to do a favour to a Serb neighbour than a Muslim neighbour. They would always welcome Serb neighbours and serve them better than Muslim neighbours until those political parties came on the scene. And now this difference in appearance, you couldn't tell who is who. But what is hidden inside, nobody can tell either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We must hurry-up if you don't want to come back next week. What I want to say, Mr. Crncalo, is the fact that if some soldiers were coming back from the front or going back to the front, and it doesn't say on your forehead that you were a Muslim, and even if it did say so, whether a Muslim was killed at Pale by some such soldiers -- not at Pale --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the street but in the prison they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to depict a picture from the 6th of April right up to the 12th of June. We have a situation whereby at Pale there were at least as many refugees as there were local inhabitants, and we saw that the municipality was doing its best to provide food and limit smugglers and war profiteers from smuggling in food, and so on. They were rationing food, stipulating how much could be bought by one person, and forbidding tradesmen from putting up prices unreasonably, and they charged one company to be in charge of selling food, and so on. Then weapons were handed in and some weapons were not. And do you know how they know that? Because they arrested Senaid Memic and "hodza" Glivaja [phoen] owned up. So the police knew how many weapons there were. In this second wave, the police were going hand in hand with the army to collect up the weapons and in Renovica --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The accused should come to his question immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's stop the speech and put your question. If you are going to put your case, just be brief. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any refugees and what was the ratio? Were there as many refugees as there were local inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was food -- were food supplies rationed and didn't the authorities prohibit profiteers from raising prices?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about a woman from Dobrinja, she was a Serb coming into Pale and she had a 250-gram package of margarine in one hand and 2 or 3 kilos of potatoes in the on the other hand. And I asked her, Where did you buy that? And she said, I didn't buy it, it was being distributed. So she said, How am I going to survive on just this for the next week, 250 grams of margarine and 2 or 3 kilos of potatoes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was she a Serb?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, when the first call came up, were quantities of weapons handed over?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the urban part of Pale, the people there in the space of two hours, everybody got together and handed in their weapons to the police station. Now, I can't say what happened in Praca, Renovica, and Podgrab and so on, in those other villages lower down. I told you how I moved around Pale and what happened in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you confirmed that there was an ultimatum, that people were killed, and that after these policemen were killed, Malko Koroman made the ultimatum over television with tears in his eyes and then a second wave of handing in weapons took place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked to slow down for the benefit of one and all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please put a pause. I know you are hurrying, but don't forget the hard work of the interpreters. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like to express my respect for the interpreters and to apologise to them, and I'm sure they understand me too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We know that the families suffered, the four people were killed, the others fled, their property was seized, their houses burnt, their cattle seized, and then we come to Zlovrh, 40 dead; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about Zlovrh. Where is this place, Zlovrh?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's the incident when they were killed in Zepa in an ambush, they were killed in an ambush, they were tricked. Although they were told that they could take food to the crew at the relay station at Zlovrh and that was a relay station that catered to all of us, the whole population. And that was where you saw me, that's called Zlovrh.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I comment? One Serb fighter said on television, when he was transported by helicopter from Zepa to Pale, can I tell you what he said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer my questions, otherwise you will stay on next week too. So it would be better for you to just stick to answering my questions. Anyway, that was the situation in which the president of the municipality, Radislav Starcevic was his name, and Slobodan Kacevic [phoen] was the man before him, he couldn't take it anymore so he left that position. But he wrote this document 1D833, the one I'd like to have called up now. We have the document on our screens. The date is the 12th of June, 1992, which means that after all these events, the president of the Pale municipality is writing to the secretary of the Serbian Democratic Party of Pale. And this is what he says: "As the president of the Assembly, I am requesting that you urgently call a meeting of the Main Board of the SDS of Pale in order for the party to adopt a general position on the moving out of non-Serbs from Pale municipality: "I would like to point out that unless the Main Board meets as soon as possible, or rather, if the Main Board meets as possible we can call a session of the Assembly for the 18th of June, 1992, which is a Thursday." So let me help you out here and tell you that Mr. Starcevic had to call for a session, not to have to wait for the regular session, because the work of the Serbian Democratic Party was put on ice, and he didn't know what to do with respect to this question of moving out. So can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Starcevic wrote this as a reaction to the state organs on the basis of his meeting with you, or rather, the representatives of the Muslim community and the demands they made. So he is calling for an institutional solution to this question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see the document. This is the first time that I'm looking at it. I've never seen it before. I know that we did not ask to move out. We asked to be provided safety and security in remaining in Pale municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in the meantime, Mr. Crncalo, after all these critical events, you asked - and we have the document - you asked that you be allowed to dislocate, to move to another area. You're right there. And I'd like to make the difference under our law. A place of residence is something permanent and "boravak" is temporary residence. So Mr. Crncalo is right. They asked for a temporary change of residence because they did not get a permanent change of residence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender 1D833 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- what is your answer, Mr. Crncalo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We asked to be allowed to stay in Pale in our houses, to continue living where we had always lived, but we were told that we couldn't remain. At the last meeting, we were told that we couldn't stay in our houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you of 1D832, where we -- you were granted the request to move out and relocate [as interpreted]. So that's not right what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a pity that the meeting wasn't filmed, the meeting attended by the late Nikola Koljevic, then you'd be able to see whether that was so or not. And I wasn't alone there. I'd like to tell you to bring all the people in -- if you were to bring all the people in the courtroom that were there, they would all say the same thing that I'm telling you now, if you were to bring them in from the streets and bring them into court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to make an intervention to the transcript on page 77, line 7, [In English] "You were granted the request to move," [Interpretation] No, no, that's a mistake there. You were told that there was no need for you to move out. Your request was to move out, but the document states that you were not permitted to do so but were encouraged to stay, to remain, and that was on the 11th of April.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I survived all these events, the events that you're talking about now, and you cannot persuade me and convince me that we left voluntarily. You'll understand me. What did we take with us? We took only what we could carry in our two hands, that's all. Nobody asked us, What's going to happen to your homes, to your houses, to your cars? All you could do was take what you could carry with you, so we were almost bare-handed, homeless, penniless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's move on. I think we dealt with this issue when you were putting that document to the witness. Let's move on to the next issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have 1D834 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in the meantime, I'd like to remind you, Mr. Crncalo, of paragraph 67 of your own amalgamated statement where you say: [In English] "A number of times we did talk to the chief of police and the president of municipality. When the first convoy left towards Sarajevo, a day or two afterwards, we went to see the municipality president and ask him again what had happened to those people, why did those people have to leave that have you done -- what have you done to the people. And I said," [Interpretation] And you're quoting, [In English] "They must have infringed upon the law, in some way done something unlawful." [Interpretation] So that's what you said. Now I'd like to draw your attention to the next document, 1D834, which is on our screens. We saw that on the 12th of June, the president informed the people that they could call -- convene a meeting in six days' time, and these are the minutes from that session of the Municipal Assembly of Pale. If we look at paragraph 3 it says that: "The session was chaired by the president of the Pale Municipal Assembly Radislav Starcevic." And then going down the page: "Before moving on to the proposed agenda, the member of the Pale Municipal Assembly and others present observed a minute of silence in honour of the memory of the Pale soldiers who had died at Zepa." And then we have the agenda, the first item was the security situation in the municipality and then sub-items. Item number 2 was to take a stand -- that the municipality should take a stand on the moving out of non-Serbs from the territory of Pale municipality. Then let's move on to the next page. Item 1, the security situation and a report from the brigade command. Paragraph 2, it says: "Objections from soldiers who fled from Sarajevo with their families, they claim that they're being treated as second-rate citizens. So they fled Sarajevo, left their lovely flats, left with nothing, were placed in units, and then that they were being treated as second-class citizens." So they have the same impression that you had, but, of course, the municipality couldn't resolve the question and the situation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how they felt. I know how I felt and what it was like for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you can see it was difficult for the Serbs of Sarajevo as well. And now let's move on to item 7, the penultimate page. Item 7, please. Item 7 of the agenda, the conclusion is that: "In these war time conditions, all forms of crime should be prevented as well as war time profiteering and that the public security station of Pale should be engaged and the municipal authority of inspection." So that was item -- or the seventh conclusion under item 1, in actual fact. Now we come to item 2, and this relates to the question of relocation: "Linked to the problem of moving out of the territory of the municipality, the Muslims, opinions were divided on the issue with respect to the manner in which it was being done and the justifications for it. "Assemblyman Obrad Kljajic considered that the government should first pass a decision on the issue and that the municipalities should then act in accordance with the decision made. "Arsen Jugovic was of the opinion that all those who had found an exchange and signed exchange contracts should be allowed to leave. "Moving out with the help of UNPROFOR and exchanges were also stated as a possibility. "Milorad Gazivoda gave a constructive proposal and said that this process of moving out should be done on a voluntary basis. "The president of the Assembly and the chairman of the executive committee objected to the activities of the public security station in this respect because it had participated in an attempt to organise the Muslims and move them out which was done without a political decision having been taken which meant that the official structures of power and authority had been bypassed. So for this reason, the attempt was prevented and stopped. "To avoid going into an overly broad discussion, the Assembly decided that a commission formulate the proposal on the mode of evacuation of Muslim or Croat population underlying the principle of voluntariness and organised manner of moving out. "This working group is to be nominated."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We have absolutely no objection to this document coming in. Your Honours can read it in your own time. There's only 30 minutes left in this session. I'm just slightly concerned about conducting some re-direct of the witness and permitting him to leave today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fully understood. Mr. Karadzic, as I said to you, put your question. We can read this document. Just put the crux of your question, and I would like you to conclude your cross-examination in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I was reckoning until a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, there was one attempt the authorities stopped, and I tried to deal with this by decisions of the proper authorities. Just tell me, did you know about this or not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this. I knew about other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document, 1D834. And can I now call up 1D835 to speed things up a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you don't have to come again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D31.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will explain while we're waiting. This is a decision of the next day, 19 June, where the president of the municipality, Radislav Starcevic follows up on the Assembly decision and formulates his own decision. It is called decision on the mode of relocation of citizens of Muslim and Croatian ethnicity. This is relocation, not a change of residence and not evacuation or moving out. It says -- let me now read: "The citizens of Muslim and Croatian ethnicity who wish to change," et cetera, et cetera. Did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But what do you call moving out? To us it meant deportation, expulsion of people from their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you make statements like this, I'll ask for you to stay another week.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let it be a year, if need be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot just skip over the following documents, Your Excellencies. Let us move on to the protection of property and what happened to the property left behind by Muslims at Pale. There are so many things that are left untackled with this witness. I can't leave it at that. Can I tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the exhibit number for 835?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call 1D844, and it's also Prosecution document P11231.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, under 775, dated 2 July 1992, we read: "Contract: Sulejman Crncalo and Taib Crncalo give their house in Pale in," such and such a street, "to Dragica Subotic," such and such a street. Do you dispute that this is yours?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not disputing it, I signed this, but under duress.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll have to clarify every detail then. 1D845, please. Mr. Crncalo, this is the contract about this temporary exchange of properties, and it's temporary because the government banned any trade in real estate for the duration of the war and it did so in April. The government banned this trade temporarily because it couldn't have been honest. This is written on a typewriter. "Sulejman and Taib Crncalo," the original is unclear, the English is better, "exchange a residential house and auxiliary buildings and accompanying land with Dragica Subotic." Article 4: "The contracting parties hereby undertake that the use and safe-keeping of the property on the contract shall be temporary and last until the end of the war until the conditions for normal life are restored, at which time the final status of the property and the contract shall be resolved by agreement with the mandatory consent of the contracting parties." And 5: "The contracting parties shall take possession of the contracted property and undertake to maintain them in their current condition and all necessary obligations must be settled before a final agreement." This was a contract typed for you and signed by your brother Taib and even you. We have your signature here. And it was signed by Dragica Subotic. She signed in Cyrillic script, you signed in Latinic script. So there was no coercion, nor was it a permanent exchange. On the basis of this contract, after the war, you could, at any time say, Give me back my property.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone who refused to sign such a contract had to hand in their keys to their house to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me one example.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the information that circulated among the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who produced this information?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you about the activists who went from house to house, Jovan Skobo and Kojic, Radomir, you denied it when I said it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have evidence about that as well. You are dealing with the state authority here, a state authority verifying your contract. And you can see that they're not even letting you exchange the property because the government had banned sale of real estate for the duration of the war. This copy of the contract which is also available to the Prosecution is hereby tendered, 1D845.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Previous document is number what, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit D33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this contract is ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, the contract is D33 and the previous Exhibit was P735.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the 844 is exhibit number what? We didn't deal with it when we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it he's tendering that as well and the witness confirmed. That is D33 and then this contract will be D34 then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That's correct. With the proviso that this excerpt from the municipal register was recognised by the witness and the Prosecution also has it as an exhibit. Now I'd like to call up 1D834, and I won't be tendering it. For the time being, I just want to show the contract of the other contracting party on the same transaction. It's actually number 843.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I can already indicate that we object to this statement. It doesn't comply with 92 bis or 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not intend to offer it for admission. I just want to confront Mr. Crncalo with the testimony of the other contracting party. If necessary, we will tender this statement according to appropriate procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 2, you can see that this is the statement of Miro Subotic. His father's name is Milanko, and he's the son of the Dragica Subotic with whom you had made that agreement. He says here, after his personal details, that they had a family house in Pofalici which they abandoned after the attack of Muslim armed forces on Pofalici in May 1992: "After being expelled from our own home, we fled to Pale using byroads and tracks via Zuc and Rajlovac." You know that over 350 Serbs were killed on that occasion in Pofalici. I don't want your response: "In Pale, we found accommodation in a weekend cottage owned by our family, who had also fled from their homes in Sarajevo. "We stayed there for about a month because my mother Dragica found out that exchanges were possible then between local population and those who had fled from Sarajevo. Muslims tended to view Sarajevo as an ideal, like Serbs view Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused slow down, please, when reading especially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters were not able to interpret what you said. Slow down and starting from the part: "My mother met Taib Crncalo ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But you have to believe me, I can't leave anything unclear and we are very pressed for time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The next day, together with my mother, I came to Taib who was accompanied by his brother Sulejman, and there on the spot we agreed to swap houses. The same day we went to the building of the Municipal Assembly of Pale and there we made and signed an agreement on exchange. This was on 2nd July 1992. It was very crowded in the municipal building on that day because many citizens were drafting and having verified similar contracts on property exchange. The house that we temporarily received for use was on 1316 Muslim Brigade street and was owned by brothers Taib and Sulejman Crncalo from Pale. "The signed contract obligated both parties to take of the properties which can clearly be seen from the original contract on exchange that I have attached thereto. "The brothers Taib and Sulejman, together with a large number of their countrymen, left Pale in an organised fashion in a bus convoy, probably on the same day. They all left voluntarily at their own request and without suffering any mistreatment. "I personally helped Taib and Sulejman carry their things to the bus. We parted on friendly terms and Sulejman's allegations which you have confronted me with that someone threatened them and forced them out of their house are not true." I have read this because this is not going to be tendered now: "My brother and I with our families lived in the house together with our mother in this -- during the war. After the war" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think you are able to put a question now to the witness whether he confirms or knows about the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did Miro Subotic help you carry your luggage to the bus?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he helped my late brother. He didn't help me, certainly. But he wasn't there, he wasn't present when we signed this contract on exchange. He didn't even accompany us on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The interpretation is not correct. It's true that -- didn't you say he helped your brother?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't see whether he helped my brother, but he certainly didn't help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the first time his mother was without him. On the next day he came to you and Taib. So we are both right. The first time he wasn't there, the second time he was?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't both be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were two meetings?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my late brother and Dragica, I went to the municipal building. He was there, but still he didn't sign anything. His mother signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, a paragraph which the accused omitted reading reads like this: "My mother met Taib Crncalo in front of his house in the part of Pale that was predominantly inhabited by Muslims with the help of some acquaints from Sarajevo who had already exchanged their homes. There she," his mother, "she reached a verbal agreement with Taib regarding the exchange of property. This house was owned by Taib and Sulejman"; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Conclude your cross-examination in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, there was no police present. You were alone all the time. There were no official authorities when you were negotiating the deal?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was police present on the road when we were moving towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document 1D850, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, I will describe what the document is about. The municipal authorities of Pale, on the 14th of July, that's 12 days after your contract, make an initiative. And it says in the conclusion: "Bearing in mind that the central commission and subcommission for listing and registering movable and immovable property of citizens of non-Serb ethnicity who had fled the area of the municipality failed to do their job in full, so there had been theft and unlawful disposal of abandoned properties, the Executive Board did not accept the report of the said commissions, and concluded to form an auditing commission with the following task: "To review the way property of -- non-Serb property is used household by household. "2. To seal all residential and auxiliary buildings which were abandoned and did not change ownership by legal contract and have no one responsible to prevent any damage to these buildings." You can read it for yourself. I have no time. I want to conclude. In the middle of the war, in the middle of the problems with all the refugees and shortages and everything, the municipality is unhappy with the work of the commission but forms instead an auditing commission to protect non-Serb properties. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to address the Court. Why are you reading this to me, who left that municipality and my home? What kind of comment do you want from me? I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you dealt with the topic. Now my last question. Is that right? I don't have any more time? Is that right? Perhaps one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, how many Muslims lived in Pale municipality, 4 and a half to 5.000?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-three per cent in percentages, according to the census lists that I had a chance to see, about 5.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many left Sarajevo, 1.042?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, part of Pale municipality and Renovica and a few villages in Pale municipality, that's what was left. The other people gravitating towards Sarajevo, everybody left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Document 1D836 next, please. 1836 [as interpreted] is a report dated the 6th of July, 1992, about checking out the place of temporary residence for Muslims and Croats from the municipality in the Stari Grad municipality, and you said, yourself, these are neighbouring municipalities. And the conclusion was, or rather, the report said that up until the third, or rather, with five buses on the 3rd of July, 324 citizens left and before that on the 1st of July and the 2nd of July, 220. The total number is 1.042 out of 5.000. So if you deduct 1.042 from 5.000, that means three-quarters of the Muslims stayed on in Pale municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. Your figures are not right. There couldn't have been that many inhabitants in Renovica, the villages are Strane, Datelj [phoen], Komrani, and that was all, those three villages and the urban area of the Renovica commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
