utterances.text: Well, this is a state document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then it's not a good one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender 1D836 and call up 1D842 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I was told that the previous document used 1D844 is the one which is identical to the one of the Prosecution exhibits, so there's no need to admit it again. So, therefore, document 1D845 will be Exhibit D33, and 1D850 will be Exhibit D34, and the current document 1D836 is Exhibit -- admitted as Exhibit D35. And that should be the last examination on your part, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I might be allowed one more document. Can I tender one more document, offer up one more document, 1D829 without reading it, it's about Pofalici, of the 17th of May, from where Subotic comes who reached an agreement about the exchange of properties or the use of property with Mr. Crncalo. 1D829 is the document referring to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, do you object to the admission of 1D829?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, no, we do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit it as Exhibit D36, and then I'll give you the witness for your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to move very quickly on this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted one more document. Could I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What document is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D830, in which we can see -- well, it's linked to this previous document, and in it, we can see that the houses in Pofalici were blown up, mined, and it corresponds to something that was said in his statement. So this is the 22nd of May, a document about the blowing up of Serb houses in Pofalici. And I would give up on the rest, although there would be much more that I would like to have been able to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President, and in respect of other documents which he has not had a chance to -- we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we will not admit them. So we'll admit the document 1D830 as Exhibit D37. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, in your -- in the cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic was asking you about a speech which he gave in Pale in June of 1992, and he was referring to your evidence in the Krajisnik trial about that speech. And it was put to you that in your evidence there you didn't mention a single word about the actual content of that speech. Now, first of all, Mr. Karadzic referred to three pages in the Krajisnik transcript, 5294, 5327, and 5342. I want to point out for the record that 5294 was part of the Prosecution's oral summary of the witness's evidence in the Krajisnik case. I just want to briefly put to you, Mr. Crncalo, your evidence at page 5327. You had been questioned for some time about the meeting which you attended with Malko Koroman and Nikola Koljevic. And then it was put to you: "Now when you say," this is at line 9 on page 5327. "Q. Now, when you say 'after the second half of March,' are you talking about when the Serb government came to Pale or are you talking about when the meeting took place or both? "A. The Serb government had moved to Pale before that, prior to the meeting at which Nikola Koljevic turned up, and I can conclude this because I had the opportunity of seeing Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic at Pale. "Q. In person on TV? "A. Well, as far as -- well, maybe I've got that mixed up. If I said 'Krajisnik,' no I did not see Krajisnik, I saw Koljevic, that's what I meant. He came to the meeting. As for Karadzic, I saw him in front of the cultural centre when he delivered a speech there. "Q. This meeting took place before or after you were arrested on March the 2nd of 1992? "A. Afterwards, after my arrest." Now, during that portion of your evidence, were you questioned about the content of Mr. Karadzic's speech?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you asking me whether they asked me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm asking you whether, in that part of your evidence in Krajisnik, whether anyone was questioning you about what exactly Mr. Karadzic had said.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me or questioned me about it or asked me for any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to move briefly to page 5342 of the Krajisnik transcript at line 5. Now, at this stage in your evidence you had been questioned, Mr. Crncalo, about the presence of Serb paramilitary men in Pale, and it was put to you as follows: "Q. Now, you mentioned earlier, I think, that there was a time prior to May and June when the Republika Srpska government had relocated its headquarters to Pale. Do you know where in Pale their headquarters were located? "A. As far as I could tell, the TV station was also close to the culture centre, and on one occasion I saw Mr. Karadzic delivering a speech there. So judging by all that, I would say that they were in the culture centre." Now, in that part of your evidence, Mr. Crncalo, did anyone ask you expressly what Mr. Karadzic had said?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember anybody asking me exactly what Karadzic said, but maybe they did. I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to my final topic, and that concerns -- a number of questions were put to you about the morgue where you discovered the body of your wife and of other persons who had been killed in the Markale market explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And I would like, if possible, the Registrar to bring up 65 ter number 10344, page 31 in B/C/S and page 35 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like you to look, Mr. Crncalo, at the document on the right on the screen in front of you, if you can.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know what that document is?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an extract from the hospital about the death of my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you know who signed that document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was signed by -- well, I don't know the man, but I heard that he was a medical expert and that his name was Ilijas Dobraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That document is dated 28th of August, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and that was the day of the massacre in Sarajevo at the Markale market, as has been documented here, and it says Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, that ends my re-examination. I would like to tender that document which forms a part of 43 autopsy certificates relating to the 43 victims of the Markale II incident. I would like to tender the entire document, the entire collection. All of the autopsy certificates are in the same form. The cause of death is different in -- depending on which autopsy certificate, but they're all in the same form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I would prefer to take it one by one. This was a separate incident. Because I'd like to look through them. I'm a doctor myself, and this man Dobraca was a colleague of mine. So I would like to see what all this is about. But I'm sure we'll be able to accept everything in the end, once we look through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I'm not challenging this, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit it with the caveat that we will marked for identification with regard to the remaining part other than this part. I think that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P740.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Crncalo, this concludes your evidence. Again, I thank you very much, on behalf of the Tribunal, for your coming to the Tribunal to give it. You're now free to go. I hope you make a safe trip back to your home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It was my moral duty to come. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be given an explanation, Your Excellency, just one explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have to rise, given the next -- in light of the next session, so we'll hear from you next week, Wednesday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
